newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close off lows after Wall St bounces.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close off lows after Wall St bounces.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed sharply lower on Tuesday, but were off lows in line with Wall Street and bonds after a nervous and occasionally volatile session.
World financial markets were hit by news of a U.S. missile attack on Iraq. This, coupled with fears that U.S. rates might rise more than originally anticipated, dragged bourses lower.
The general index fell 2.44 points, 0.69 percent, to 352.01 and the Ibex shed 29.56 points, 0.73 percent, to 4,004.00.
Telefonica managed to reverse earlier losses, ending up 5 pesetas to 2,340 supported by strong first half results and an upgraded recommendation from Goldman, dealers said.
Firms which have performed well up to recently-reported first half figures were the worst hit amid general selling.
Two such were food distribution chain Pryca, which fell 115 pesetas to 2,955 and property group Metrovacesa which dropped 55 pesetas to 4,155.

Dealers said that aside from events abroad, the bourse should be supported by concrete details on the 1997 budget, due to be announced before the end of the month. Up to then prices may be volatile, and particularly sensitivity to foreign news.
